title: Cineac, Duiker's newsreel cinema
check_note: Google Maps (Nov 2026) lists 'Cineac Amsterdam', a cultural association, at no. 31; no news on the new use. Who uses it, and the canopy and booth window, need a look.

title: Door wind bewogen beweging, Wicher Meursing's last wind sculpture
check_note: In 2022 the vanes barely moved; whether it swings freely again is not known.

title: Hamer- en Bouwershofje, two old hofjes moved to the city's edge
check_note: Okura staff use also in nl.wikipedia and amsterdamopdekaart.nl, but no source dated after July 2018 (search 24 Nov 2026). Confirm on site.

title: Huis met de Neuzen (the House with the Noses)
check_note: The register says three caricature heads; whether all three are still in place and where exactly on the front was not checked.

title: Keizersgracht 516, Bodon's glass bookshop
check_note: After Borzo left (June 2021) the space hosted short exhibitions as Art Space Keizersgracht 516 (June 2022, May 2024, Instagram). Use in 2026 not found.

title: Lokaal 't Loosje and its brewery tile wall
check_note: The horse-tram waiting room and the origin of the name rest on the café's own account; an archive photo or tram history would settle them.

title: Odeon, from brewery to concert hall to gay disco
check_note: Supper Dining & Club runs the club-restaurant at no. 460 (Google Maps listing, open, Nov 2026). Still to check: whether the lamb is still on the gable.

title: Reestraat 6, where Anton de Kom lived
check_note: No plaque for De Kom is known; check whether one is on the front.

title: Swigtershofje
check_note: Chapel confirmed as a guest suite (Nov 2026). Owner: sold 1978 to Stichting Leefklimaat, 1991 to De Key (hofjesinamsterdam, 2018); nothing later found. Whether the gate is ever open not confirmed.

title: Walenweeshuis, the Walloon orphanage waiting for a future
check_note: Amended exterior restoration permit granted 19 Dec 2025 (Z2025-038483); no report found that works have started (25 Nov 2026). Check for scaffolding, a permit notice, and any public access.

title: Beta berlayar jauh, the Moluccan marines' monument
check_note: Marineterrein news and the Stadscuratorium advice (12 May 2026) say only 'the Voorwerf'; not in the city art register (Nov 2026). Pin still an estimate.

title: De Swarte Mvele and the De Vries van Buuren building (Waterlooplein 3)
check_note: Pin is near the corner of Waterlooplein 3; set it on the stone in the Zwanenburgwal side wall

title: Kattenburgerplein, the old fronts that are new
check_note: Which numbers form the reconstructed row is not stated in the sources; pin at nos. 56-59, where the stone De Groenne Oven is.

title: Leprozenpoort and the Grenspaal: the lepers' gate that moved, and a turtle carrying city debris
check_note: Pin on the address point of Sint Antoniesluis 22; the gate stands on the front of nos. 21-24, check which spot.

title: Mbulu Ngulu, an African guardian of the dead on an advertising column
check_note: The city art register (Nov 2026) still gives the 1991 spot on the Czaar Peterstraat; the pin is on the reported new spot. Confirm the column on site.

title: Nieuwezijds Kolk, the castle under the street
check_note: No marker known; pin from the dig plan on the Kolk. Check on site for any sign in the paving.

title: Plukbos, the food forest behind the Wittenburg blocks
check_note: Pin on the garden in the inner court; which street gate is the main way in is not confirmed.

title: The Dam shooting of 7 May 1945 and its 32 name stones
check_note: Pin on the 4en5mei point for the stones; the 1947 plaque is on the corner of the Kalverstraat.

title: The bicycle garage under the water at Stationsplein
check_note: Pin on the garage itself; the spot of the Lex Horn walls inside is not known.

title: The garden house that moved behind Keizersgracht 62
check_note: Stadsherstel (Nov 2026) gives the current user as Stichting Euro Business Center; no open-day opening of the garden house found. Pin approximate, behind the houses.

title: The rooster of De Haan's matzo factory (Valkenburgerstraat)
check_note: Sources differ on where inside the stone hangs (the hall of the flats or the parking garage entrance) and whether it can be seen from outside

title: Tip Top, the Jewish quarter's theatre (gone)
check_note: Pin placed on the old theatre site; set it on the stained-glass windows in the academy's front once seen

title: Walk of Pride, queer names from the Dam to the Homomonument
check_note: Pin at the Dam end of the Raadhuisstraat; fix it on Jillis Bruggeman's first tile. The city (video, July 2026) counts 52 tiles; the foundation says 'ruim 50'.

title: Zeelandbank, a thank-you bench from Schouwen-Duiveland
check_note: The bench was moved deeper into the Tweede Weteringplantsoen in the 2026 redesign; pin placed in the park, exact spot to confirm.

title: Cotton Club, the Nieuwmarkt's Surinamese jazz café
check_note: Google Maps lists it with hours and reviews to Oct 2026, but the unit was offered to let (Apr 2025) and for sale. No press or own-site confirmation; settle on site.

title: Elizabeth Wolffschool, a public school for paying girls
check_note: The register (about 2005) says it is still a school, run privately; check what uses the building now.

title: O Johnny, the gaper that replaced a gaper
check_note: Drugstore Het Heertje closed in spring 2024; the gaper was photographed in June 2024, and a blog post of 1 Sep 2026 shows it again. No dated authoritative source yet.

title: Roetershofje, behind a door on the Lindengracht
check_note: Only historical sources; check on site whether a court with six small houses survives behind Lindengracht 171-187.

title: The Kogelbron, a granite ball floating on water
check_note: Photographed in October 2018; check the fountain still runs and the ball still turns.

title: The first Tooneelschool building, Marnixstraat 150
check_note: Studios confirmed by nl.wikipedia (2023) and amsterdamopdekaart.nl (last updated November 2025); nothing later found 24 Nov 2026.

title: The neighbourhood embroidery on the Weesperstraat (Weesperstraat 100)
check_note: Hung outdoors June 2024 (Parool 29 Jun 2024); latest Street View at the corner is May 2024, before it went up; no dated image of the wall since. Needs a look on site.

title: The phone box library of the Boomstraat
check_note: Latest dated report is November 2021; confirm the box and its spot (pinned at no. 67).

title: Trompettersteeg, the narrowest alley and its hidden coat of arms
check_note: No evidence of the coat of arms or the sailors after 2021; check both on site.

title: Walraven van Hall's snapped tree and the Navalny memorial, Frederiksplein
check_note: Still in the city art register (Nov 2026), but no dated photo after 2018. Confirm the acacia survived the 2020-2025 rebuild.
